title: What can you say about acetyl-L-carnitine in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 1 wording for acetyl-L-carnitine; the strongest is "Helps support cognitive health and brain function" (moderate, 1.5-4 g a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats dementia or Alzheimer's disease".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps support cognitive health and brain function.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 1.5-4 g a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 1.5-4 g of acetylcarnitine a day.
supported_wordings.form: Acetylcarnitine from a source on Health Canada's list (such as acetyl L-carnitine hydrochloride), counted as acetylcarnitine

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Cognitive Function Products

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: Health Canada monograph: Cognitive Function Products

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
